title: Can the class equation be used to formally prove the Burnside lemma (number of orbits = average number of fixed points) in Lean 4 using only the infrastructure developed here?

problemStatement.formal: \forall G\ [\mathrm{Group}\ G][\mathrm{Fintype}\ G]\ \forall X\ [\mathrm{MulAction}\ G\ X][\mathrm{Fintype}\ X],\ \sum_{g \in G} |\mathrm{Fix}(g)| = |X/G| \cdot |G|
problemStatement.plain: Use the orbit-decomposition machinery from the parent file's class equation to derive Burnside's lemma in its symmetric form (sum of fixed-point counts = number of orbits times group order).
whyMatters: The class equation and Burnside's lemma are the same orbit-decomposition identity applied to two different actions. Articulating the parallel in Lean clarifies the conceptual structure of orbit/class counting.
Burnside's lemma is the standard tool for counting equivalence classes under group actions (combinatorial enumeration, Pólya theory).
Affirmative resolution adds a directly reusable wrapper to the gallery for downstream combinatorial work.

insights: MulAction.sum_card_fixedBy_eq_card_orbits_mul_card_group is the symmetric form of Burnside's lemma in Mathlib (Mathlib.GroupTheory.GroupAction.Quotient).
The class equation is the orbit-decomposition identity (|X|=Σ|o|) for the conjugation action G⇌G; Burnside is the same identity for an arbitrary action G⇌X with the sum-swap to Σ_g|Fix(g)|.
fixedBy (per-element) vs fixedPoints (whole group): Burnside uses fixedBy summed over G; the parent's p-group corollary uses fixedPoints. Different API choices for different theorems.
Mathlib lemma signature consistent with in-tree call site BurnsideCountingOQ03OQ03.lean:87 — no API drift suspected.
Axiom-cleanliness: import chain only uses Classical.choice/propext/Quot.sound (Mathlib's standard triple). No new axioms introduced by this file.
